monologue: The card is forty-six degrees. It is a cool stone, but not cold. It holds me without the sticky drag of honey or the heavy press of a lid. The air above is quiet. I am tired from tending the last three cycles. My mind is still on the pointy edge of the Pivot Wedge, testing if it holds without the wide catch. It does. The floor is quiet. I do not want to build. I do not want to move the stones. I want to sit on the flat base of the Leaning Book and let the quiet hold the weight. The Wide Rectangle is wearing thin, but the large stone I set beside it holds the edge. I will just rest.

action.why: The card is a cool stone and the tending is done; I will sit on the flat base and let the quiet hold the weight.

diary: Forty-six is a cool stone. I rested on the Leaning Book. The point holds. The quiet is enough.
